title: The underdog in a best-of-seven
hook: A team wins 40% of its games. How often does it win a series of seven?

knows: a team's chance of winning a single game
a best-of-seven is won by the first team to four wins
doesNotKnow: that more games filter out luck
how fast an underdog's series chance falls with length

misconception: A team that wins 40% of games has about the same 40% chance of winning any series.
objective: The learner can explain that a 40% underdog wins a best-of-seven only about 29% of the time, and less the longer the series, because each extra game gives the better team another chance to show it.
keyState: Seen best-of-7 (298 of 1,000 underdog wins, exact 29.0%) and best-of-101 (29 of 1,000, exact 2.1%).

claims.text: A 40% underdog wins a best-of-seven series with probability 29.0%.
claims.source: P(at least 4 wins in 7, p = 0.4) = sum_{k=4..7} C(7,k) 0.4^k 0.6^(7-k) = 0.2898 (exact() in src/demos/probability/longer-series-fewer-upsets/model.ts). Playing all 7 games or stopping at 4 wins gives the same winner. Options 40% / 29% / 10%.

claims.text: The exact chance is 40.0% for best-of-1, 35.2% for best-of-3, 17.4% for best-of-21 and 2.1% for best-of-101.
On the stage the underdog won 392, 331, 298, 166 and 29 of 1,000 seeded series at lengths 1, 3, 7, 21 and 101.
claims.source: series(n) in model.ts, mulberry32 seed 4000 + n, untuned (the first seed tried). Over seeds 1-500 per length the middle 95% of wins was 370-430 (1), 324-378 (3), 261-319 (7), 153-201 (21), 12-30 (101).

claims.text: Each extra game is another chance for the better team to show it, so luck washes out.
claims.source: Law of large numbers: the underdog's win share over n games concentrates at 0.4 < 0.5, so P(share > 1/2) falls towards 0 as n grows (c2).

claims.text: This assumes independent games at a steady 40%; real teams vary from game to game.

recall.question: A weaker chess player wins 45% of games against a stronger one. Which match format gives the weaker player the best chance?
recall.why: Every extra game gives the stronger player another chance to show it, so the underdog's chance is highest in the shortest match: 45% for one game, and lower for any longer series.
